Awake, ye saints; to praise your King,
Your pious pleasure, while you sing,
No line of this stanza quotes a verse closely; it is the hymn's own confession.
Watts made this hymn from Psalm 135, "in the language of the New Testament": a paraphrase, not a translation. The line that comes closest to it is marked.

1Hallelujah! Praise the name of the LORD. Give praise, O servants of the LORD, 2who stand in the house of the LORD, in the courts of the house of our God. 3Hallelujah, for the LORD is good; sing praises to His name, for it is lovely. 4For the LORD has chosen Jacob as His own, Israel as His treasured possession. … 17 more verses PSALM 135 · ITS FIRST VERSES · BEREAN STANDARD BIBLE READ PSALM 135
Heaven, earth, and sea, confess his hand; He bids the vapours rise; Lightning and storm at his command Sweep thro' the sounding skies. STANZA III
